name: Johnnie Walker
desc: Scotch whisky brand owned by Diageo, with Red, Black, Double Black, Green, Gold and Blue Label expressions sold worldwide.
markets: Sold in around 180 countries through Diageo's global distribution; strongest in Asia, the Americas and Europe; Diageo is listed in London.
rationale: Premium global spirits brand with a motorsport history; F1 could support hospitality and consumer activation, though alcohol advertising rules vary by market.

name: C&C Group
desc: Cider and beer maker and drinks distributor with Bulmers (Ireland), Magners, Tennent's and Menabrea brands, serving pubs and retailers.
markets: Brands and on-trade distribution centred on the UK and Ireland, with some exports; no verified expansion plans into new regions.
rationale: Strong pub and on-trade presence in Britain and Ireland suits hospitality, but reach beyond two markets makes a global F1 deal hard to justify.

name: Chateau Aroma
desc: Wine and spirits company based in Urumqi, Xinjiang, China, classified under sales and wine and spirits.
markets: Based in Xinjiang, China; customers, products and any international activity are not confirmed; assumed to serve the Chinese market.
rationale: Little is known about brand or marketing scale; an F1 link is speculative and alcohol advertising limits apply in many markets.

name: Keurig Dr Pepper
desc: North American beverage group making Keurig coffee brewers and K-Cups plus Dr Pepper, 7UP, Snapple and Canada Dry soft drinks.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States, plus Canada and Mexico; agreed in 2025 to buy JDE Peet's, which would add global coffee reach.
rationale: Large US consumer beverage portfolio with heavy marketing; F1's US growth and fan base could support a brand or product-launch partnership.

name: Accor
desc: French hotel group operating and franchising thousands of hotels under Sofitel, Pullman, Novotel, Mercure, Ibis and Fairmont brands worldwide.
markets: Hotels in about 110 countries across Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas; expanding lifestyle and luxury brands.
rationale: Global hotel and loyalty network offers hospitality, travel packages and Grand Prix market presence; rivals Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt already partner with F1.

name: Albertsons Companies
desc: US supermarket chain operating Safeway, Albertsons, Vons and Jewel-Osco stores with in-store pharmacies and a private-label food range.
markets: Stores only in the United States; no verified expansion outside the US.
rationale: Purely US grocery retailer; F1 could support Miami, Austin and Las Vegas fan promotions, but commercial fit is limited.

name: Alimentation Couche-Tard
desc: Convenience store and fuel retailer operating Circle K and Couche-Tard stores across North America, Europe and Asia.
markets: Thousands of stores in about 29 countries across North America, Europe and Asia; has pursued large acquisitions to grow further.
rationale: Circle K is a recognised consumer brand with fuel and in-store reach across North America and Europe, where F1 has strong audiences.

name: Barry Callebaut
desc: Swiss maker of chocolate and cocoa products supplying food manufacturers, chocolatiers, bakeries and restaurants worldwide.
markets: Production and customers across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa; supplies major confectionery and food groups.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with little consumer brand profile; F1 hospitality could help client entertainment, but marketing fit is modest.

name: Chobani
desc: US maker of Greek yogurt, oat milk, creamers, coffee drinks and kefir, founded by Hamdi Ulukaya.
markets: Strong in the United States, with sales in markets such as the UK and Australia; expanding product range beyond yogurt.
rationale: Consumer brand growing beyond the US; F1's US and global fan base could support brand building, though no current motorsport link is known.

name: Danone
desc: French food and beverage group making dairy and plant-based products, specialised nutrition and bottled water under Activia, Alpro and Evian.
markets: Sells in over 120 countries across Europe, North America, Asia and Latin America with large local operations.
rationale: Global consumer brands and health positioning offer product-launch and hospitality potential across F1's many host markets.

name: Jack in the Box
desc: US quick-service restaurant chain known for burgers, tacos and late-night menu items, mostly in California and Texas.
markets: Restaurants in several US states, concentrated in the West and Texas; no international footprint.
rationale: Regional US burger chain without global ambitions; F1 spend would be hard to justify against its footprint.

name: JBS
desc: Brazilian meat processor selling beef, pork, chicken and prepared foods under Seara, Swift, Friboi and Pilgrim's Pride brands.
markets: Operates and sells in North America, South America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with exports to more than 190 countries.
rationale: Mostly B2B with some consumer brands; F1 offers hospitality to trade partners and visibility in Brazil, Europe and the US.

name: Nomad Foods
desc: Frozen food company owning Birds Eye, Findus and iglo brands, selling fish, vegetables, poultry and ready meals in Europe.
markets: Sells mainly in the UK, Germany, Italy, France, Sweden and other European markets; growth through acquisitions in Europe.
rationale: Established European consumer brands could use F1 for visibility, but frozen food has limited motorsport synergy.

name: ofi (Olam Food Ingredients)
desc: Food ingredients business of Olam Group supplying cocoa, coffee, dairy, nuts and spices to food manufacturers and retailers.
markets: Sources and sells ingredients across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas, mainly to food and beverage manufacturers.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer awareness; F1 hospitality could support customer entertainment but marketing fit is modest.

name: Pilgrim's Pride
desc: Chicken producer operating processing plants in the US, Mexico, the UK and Europe, making fresh and prepared poultry products.
markets: Operations and customers in the United States, Mexico, the UK and continental Europe, selling to retailers and foodservice.
rationale: Mostly B2B commodity poultry with little consumer marketing culture; weak F1 fit.

name: Post Holdings
desc: US packaged food company with cereal brands such as Honey Bunches of Oats and Malt-O-Meal, plus refrigerated foods and foodservice.
markets: Sells mainly in North America, with the Weetabix cereal business in the UK and other markets.
rationale: Consumer cereal brands could use F1 for family audiences, but there is no obvious motorsport tie-in.

name: Wonder
desc: US food company operating food halls, restaurant brands and meal delivery, led by founder Marc Lore.
markets: Operations in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Young US food concept could use F1's US races for brand awareness, but scale is limited.

name: Grab
desc: South-East Asian super app offering ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, digital payments and financial services.
markets: Operates in Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and other South-East Asian countries.
rationale: Strong consumer brand across Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, which host or neighbour F1 races; fits regional audience and digital showcase.

name: Lineage Logistics
desc: Operator of temperature-controlled warehouses and logistics serving food producers, retailers and distributors in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
markets: Over 400 facilities in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific serving food companies and retailers.
rationale: B2B logistics brand with little consumer awareness; F1 hospitality could support client entertainment, but marketing fit is limited.

name: Diageo
desc: British spirits and beer company owning Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Guinness, Tanqueray, Don Julio and Baileys, sold worldwide.
markets: Sells in about 180 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa through a global distribution network.
rationale: Portfolio of global drinks brands suits premium hospitality and brand activation; some markets restrict alcohol advertising.

name: Froneri
desc: Ice cream maker producing own brands and Nestle brands such as Drumstick and Movenpick under licence, sold in many countries.
markets: Sells across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa through local factories and licensed Nestle ice cream brands.
rationale: Large consumer brands such as Drumstick could use F1 for activation, though sales are mostly licensed or private-label.

name: Pernod Ricard
desc: French wine and spirits group owning Absolut, Jameson, Chivas Regal, Ballantine's, Martell, Havana Club and G.H. Mumm champagne.
markets: Sells in over 160 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa, with major positions in India and China.
rationale: Already an F1 partner through Chivas Regal and G.H. Mumm; strong fit for hospitality, brand activation and Grand Prix celebrations.
f1: Chivas Regal and G.H. Mumm (Pernod Ricard brands) are listed F1 partners

name: The Magnum Ice Cream Company
desc: Ice cream maker owning Magnum, Wall's, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Algida, Klondike and Breyers, demerged from Unilever.
markets: Sells in about 100 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia, with leading brands in many markets.
rationale: Global consumer brands that could use F1 for experiential activation and sampling; no current motorsport link known.

name: Yum! Brands
desc: US restaurant franchisor owning KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and The Habit Burger & Grill with over 60,000 restaurants.
markets: Restaurants in more than 155 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, mostly franchised.
rationale: Global fast-food brands with huge reach could use F1 for fan promotions and menu launches in many Grand Prix markets.

name: Grupo Nutresa
desc: Colombian food group making cold cuts, chocolates, biscuits, coffee, ice cream and pasta under brands such as Crem Helado.
markets: Sells mainly in Colombia and other Latin American markets, with exports to the United States and other countries.
rationale: Strong Latin American consumer brands could use F1 on the region's race calendar, though no motorsport link is known.
changed: Control passed to the Gilinski group (JGDB) in 2025

name: Constellation Brands
desc: US beverage alcohol company brewing Corona, Modelo and Pacifico beers for the US market, plus wine and spirits.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States, with operations in Mexico and some presence in Canada.
rationale: Large beer brands in the US could use F1's growing American audience, though no motorsport link is known.

name: Guala Closures Group
desc: Italian maker of aluminium and plastic closures for spirits, wine, water and oil bottles, including tamper-evident designs.
markets: Plants in about 30 countries supplying drinks groups worldwide.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier with no consumer profile; F1 hospitality could help with customer entertainment, but fit is weak.

name: McCormick & Company
desc: US spice and seasoning company owning McCormick, Frank's RedHot, French's, Cholula, Old Bay and Schwartz.
markets: Sells to consumers and foodservice customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Well-known consumer brands could use F1 for sampling and restaurant partnerships, but no motorsport link is known.

name: Mondelez International
desc: Global snack company making Oreo, Cadbury, Milka, Toblerone, Ritz and Trident, sold in over 150 countries.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa with strong local brands.
rationale: Global brands with big sampling and promotion budgets suit F1's international audience and fan events.

name: Performance Food Group
desc: US foodservice distributor delivering food and supplies to restaurants, schools, hospitals and convenience stores.
markets: Distribution centres and customers across the United States; no international footprint.
rationale: B2B distributor with little consumer branding; F1 hospitality could support customers, but fit is limited.

name: Tyson Foods
desc: US producer of chicken, beef, pork and prepared foods sold to retailers, restaurants and food companies.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States, with exports to many countries and some international operations.
rationale: Large US food brand that could use F1's American races, though the commodity meat business has little motorsport synergy.

name: Subway
desc: Sandwich restaurant franchisor with thousands of locations in more than 100 countries.
markets: Franchised restaurants in over 100 countries across North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Highly visible global restaurant brand that could use F1 for fan promotions across many Grand Prix markets.

name: Zomato (Eternal)
desc: Indian online food delivery and restaurant discovery platform, now part of Eternal, also running Blinkit quick commerce.
markets: Operations centred on India; no verified expansion plans outside India.
rationale: Consumer platform with high brand visibility in India; F1 India interest is growing but there is no current Indian race.

name: AWL Agri Business
desc: Indian food and agri company known for Fortune cooking oil, also selling rice, flour, pulses and sugar.
markets: Sells mainly across India, with some exports; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Strong Indian consumer brand, but F1 has no Indian race and marketing budgets are focused on the home market.
changed: Renamed AWL Agri Business from Adani Wilmar

name: Carrefour
desc: French retail group running hypermarkets, supermarkets and convenience stores in Europe and Latin America.
markets: Stores in France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Poland, Brazil and Argentina, plus franchise operations in other countries.
rationale: Large retail brand with grocery and loyalty marketing; F1 could support promotions in Europe and Brazil.

name: McDonald's
desc: US fast-food chain franchisor with about 43,000 restaurants worldwide, serving burgers, fries and breakfast.
markets: Restaurants in over 100 countries across North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: One of the world's best-known consumer brands with deep sports sponsorship experience; F1 offers global fan reach and promotions.
f1: Arcos Dorados, McDonald's master franchisee in Latin America, is an F1 partner

name: Bloomin' Brands
desc: US restaurant group operating Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse.
markets: Restaurants mainly in the US, with Outback in Brazil and franchised restaurants in other countries.
rationale: Casual dining brand with mostly US business; F1 hospitality fit is limited.

name: Flink
desc: Berlin-based quick-commerce company delivering groceries within minutes from local dark stores via an app.
markets: Delivers in Germany and the Netherlands from local warehouses.
rationale: Fast-growing app brand with young customers; F1 could support awareness in Germany, but the business is small and loss-making.

name: Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan
desc: Indian fertilizer maker producing urea at plants in Gorakhpur, Sindri and Barauni, formed as a joint venture of state companies.
markets: Sells fertiliser within India; no international customers or expansion plans known.
rationale: State-backed fertiliser producer selling only within India with no consumer brand to market; weak F1 fit and no Indian race.

name: MBRF
desc: Brazilian food group formed by the merger of Marfrig and BRF, with brands including Sadia, Perdigao and Qualy.
markets: Sells in Brazil and over 140 countries, with large operations in South America and North America.
rationale: Large Brazilian food brands with football sponsorship history could use F1 in Brazil and for export markets.
changed: Formed in 2025 by merger of Marfrig and BRF

name: Global Eggs
desc: Privately owned holding group in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, active in egg production and egg products, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Minas Gerais, Brazil; customers and any international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Little public brand or marketing profile is known, and customers appear to be food industry buyers; an F1 partnership looks unlikely.

name: Bunge
desc: Agribusiness that buys, processes and sells oilseeds, grains and edible oils to food, feed and biofuel customers worldwide.
markets: Operates in North and South America, Europe and Asia, trading and processing crops for global customers.
rationale: B2B commodity company with little consumer branding; F1 hospitality use is possible but marketing fit is modest.

name: Molson Coors
desc: Brewer of Coors Light, Miller Lite, Molson Canadian and Blue Moon, selling in North America and Europe.
markets: Sells in the United States, Canada, the UK and Central and Eastern Europe, plus licensed brands elsewhere.
rationale: Large beer brands have sports sponsorship experience; F1 could support brand activation, subject to alcohol advertising limits.

name: COFCO Fortune
desc: Food brand and edible oil business of state-owned COFCO Group, selling cooking oil, rice, flour and packaged staples in China.
markets: Sells packaged food and cooking oil to consumers in China; no verified international expansion.
rationale: State-owned staple food brand with a mass-market Chinese focus; F1 fit is limited, though COFCO has sponsored sport elsewhere.

name: General Mills
desc: US packaged food company with Cheerios, Nature Valley, Haagen-Dazs, Pillsbury and Old El Paso brands sold in many countries.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America, with Haagen-Dazs and Old El Paso brands abroad.
rationale: Large consumer brands could use F1 for family promotions and sampling, but there is no known motorsport link.

name: Avril
desc: French agro-industrial group created by farmers' organisations, processing oilseeds and proteins into oils, feed, biofuels and food products.
markets: Operations across France, Europe, Africa and the Americas, supplying food, feed and energy customers.
rationale: Farmer-owned agro-industrial group with mostly B2B activity and little consumer branding; F1 hospitality fit is limited and marketing relevance is low.

name: Domino's Pizza
desc: Pizza delivery and carryout chain with over 21,000 stores in more than 90 countries, mostly franchised.
markets: Stores across the US, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East, many run by master franchisees.
rationale: Global consumer brand with strong digital ordering; F1 could support fan promotions across many Grand Prix markets.

name: Haldiram Snacks
desc: Indian snack maker behind Haldiram's bhujia, namkeen, sweets and ready-to-eat foods sold in shops and restaurants.
markets: Sells mainly across India, with some exports to the Indian diaspora; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Popular Indian snack brand; F1 fit is limited because it lacks an Indian race and focuses on its home market.

name: J.B. Poindexter & Co.
desc: Privately held manufacturer of truck bodies, pickup accessories and specialty vehicles, including Morgan Olson and Leer brands.
markets: Customers are fleet operators, delivery firms and dealers, mainly in the United States.
rationale: B2B vehicle equipment maker selling to fleets and dealers with little consumer marketing; weak F1 fit despite its vehicle-industry link.

name: Premium Brands Holdings
desc: Canadian food manufacturer and distributor producing specialty foods, sandwiches and protein products for retailers and foodservice customers.
markets: Sells mainly in Canada and the United States to retail and foodservice customers.
rationale: B2B-focused food manufacturer selling mostly to retailers and foodservice with little consumer branding; weak F1 fit given its Canada-US footprint.

name: Del Monte Foods
desc: US maker of canned fruit, vegetables and tomatoes sold under Del Monte, Contadina and S&W brands.
markets: Sells canned foods mainly to US retailers and consumers; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Consumer food brand in financial difficulty with a purely domestic customer base; F1 sponsorship spend is very unlikely to be approved.

name: Dine Brands Global
desc: Restaurant franchisor owning Applebee's Neighborhood Grill + Bar and IHOP, with mostly franchised US restaurants.
markets: Franchised restaurants mainly in the United States, with some in other countries.
rationale: Casual dining brands focused on US customers with franchised restaurants; F1 US races offer some visibility, but fit is limited.

name: Quirch Foods
desc: Distributor and exporter of beef, pork, poultry and seafood for supermarkets, foodservice and processors in Latin America and the US.
markets: Supplies customers in the United States, Latin America and the Caribbean from its Florida base, mainly through B2B distribution and exports.
rationale: B2B protein distributor with little consumer awareness; weak F1 fit beyond hospitality for customers.

name: Hershey
desc: US confectionery and snack maker of Hershey's chocolate, Reese's, Kit Kat (US licence) and Twizzlers.
markets: Sells mainly in North America, with business in Mexico, Brazil, India and Asia.
rationale: Strong consumer brands could use F1's US races for promotions, but there is no known motorsport link.
f1: Makes Kit Kat in the US under licence from Nestle, an F1 partner (KitKat)

name: JDE Peet's
desc: Dutch coffee and tea company selling Jacobs, Douwe Egberts, Peet's, L'OR and Tassimo in over 100 markets.
markets: Sells in over 100 markets across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Large coffee brands could use F1 for hospitality and consumer promotion in Europe and the US.
changed: Agreed to be acquired by Keurig Dr Pepper (announced 2025)

name: Equity Invest
desc: US investment company listed in food and beverage and healthcare, offering strategic investments, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Florida; holdings, customers and any international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Investment vehicle with no known consumer brand, products or international footprint; an F1 partnership looks very unlikely and the fit is weak.

name: Jersey Mike's Subs
desc: US sandwich franchisor founded in 1956, with about 3,000 restaurants serving sub sandwiches.
markets: Franchised restaurants across the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-focused sandwich brand; F1's American races could support promotions, but the business is domestic.

name: Sucro Sourcing
desc: US food ingredient processor offering sugar and sweetener sourcing, refining and supply to food manufacturers, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Florida; customers are food manufacturers, and international activity is not confirmed.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with little consumer profile and unconfirmed scale; an F1 partnership looks unlikely and the fit is weak.

name: Vilmorin & Cie (Limagrain)
desc: French vegetable and field seed company, the listed subsidiary of the Limagrain cooperative, selling seeds worldwide.
markets: Sells seeds to farmers and growers across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.
rationale: B2B seed supplier with no consumer brand and farmer customers; F1 hospitality fit is weak and marketing relevance is low.

name: Coca-Cola FEMSA
desc: Mexican bottler producing and distributing Coca-Cola drinks across Latin America, the world's largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler.
markets: Operates in Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina and other Latin American markets.
rationale: Large Latin American consumer distribution with sports sponsorship experience; F1 races in Mexico and Brazil could support activation.

name: Eroski
desc: Spanish retail cooperative running supermarkets, hypermarkets, travel agencies and fuel stations, mainly in northern Spain.
markets: Stores in Spain, concentrated in the Basque Country and northern regions.
rationale: Regional Spanish retailer with domestic focus; F1 fit is limited despite the Spanish Grand Prix.

name: B&G Foods
desc: US packaged food company with shelf-stable and frozen brands such as Green Giant, Crisco, Ortega and Cream of Wheat.
markets: Sells mainly to US and Canadian retailers and foodservice customers.
rationale: Value-focused US packaged food brands with limited marketing budgets; weak F1 fit.

name: Luckin Coffee
desc: Chinese coffee chain with more than 24,000 stores selling freshly made coffee, mostly through its app.
markets: Stores across China, with initial expansion into Singapore and the United States.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer brand with young customers; F1 could support international awareness as it expands.

name: O-I Glass
desc: Glass container maker producing bottles and jars for beverage and food companies in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
markets: Plants and customers in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific, supplying beer, wine, spirits and food producers.
rationale: B2B packaging maker with no consumer profile; F1 hospitality could support customer entertainment, but fit is weak.

name: Maple Leaf Foods
desc: Canadian packaged meats and plant-based protein company with brands such as Maple Leaf, Schneiders and Lightlife.
markets: Sells mainly in Canada and the United States, with some exports to Asia.
rationale: Domestic-focused consumer food brands; F1's Canadian Grand Prix offers some visibility, but fit is modest.

name: Roquette
desc: French family-owned maker of plant-based ingredients including starches, sweeteners, proteins and pharmaceutical excipients for food and drug makers.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia, with a US arm in North America.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier with no consumer brand and food and pharma customers; F1 hospitality fit is weak and marketing relevance is low.

name: Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages
desc: Indian bottling and distribution arm of the Coca-Cola system, making Coca-Cola, Sprite, Thums Up and Maaza for Indian retailers.
markets: Sells across India through plants and retail outlets; no operations outside India.
rationale: Mass-market Indian beverage distributor with cricket sponsorship; F1 fit is limited without an Indian race.
changed: Stake of about 40% agreed to be sold to Jubilant Bhartia group in 2025

name: Oatly
desc: Swedish oat-drink company selling oat milk, ice cream, yogurts and cooking products in Europe, North America and Asia.
markets: Sells in Europe, North America and Asia, with factories in Sweden, the Netherlands, the US and Singapore.
rationale: Brand-led plant-based consumer company that could use F1 for sustainability messaging, though it focuses on cafes and retail.

name: Fruitist
desc: Los Angeles company that designs, grows and distributes premium fruit, according to its Crunchbase description.
markets: Based in California; customers and any international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Small consumer food brand with no known international reach; weak F1 fit.

name: Rebel Foods
desc: Indian cloud kitchen company running delivery brands such as Faasos, Behrouz Biryani and Oven Story from shared kitchens.
markets: Operates in India and several Middle East markets through delivery-only restaurant brands.
rationale: Digital food brand with young customers; F1 could help brand building, but marketing budgets are limited.

name: Dmall
desc: Chinese retail technology company providing omnichannel software, fulfilment and delivery platforms to supermarkets and retailers.
markets: Serves retailers in China and Southeast Asia with retail software and fulfilment platforms.
rationale: B2B retail technology firm with limited public awareness; F1 could work as a technology showcase, but fit is modest.

name: Grupo Uvesco
desc: Spanish food retail group based in the Basque Country, operating supermarkets and a food distribution business.
markets: Stores in northern Spain only; no verified international operations or expansion plans are known for this regional supermarket group.
rationale: Regional Spanish supermarket group with limited marketing reach; F1 fit is weak despite the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.

name: Tate & Lyle
desc: British maker of specialty food and beverage ingredients, including sweeteners, fibres and texturants, for manufacturers.
markets: Sells to food and drink makers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: B2B ingredient company with little consumer visibility; F1 hospitality could support customers, but fit is limited.

name: Tesco
desc: UK's largest supermarket group, also operating in Ireland and Central Europe, with Clubcard loyalty and Tesco Mobile.
markets: Stores in the UK, Ireland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic.
rationale: Dominant UK grocery brand; F1's British fan base could support promotions, but operations are limited to Europe.

name: Starbucks
desc: World's largest coffee chain, operating and licensing cafes selling coffee, tea and food in more than 80 markets.
markets: Stores across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East, many licensed.
rationale: Global consumer brand with strong loyalty app; F1 could support fan promotions and hospitality.

name: Scandi Standard
desc: Nordic poultry producer selling chicken products under Kronfagel, Danpo, Den Stolte Hane and Naapurin Maalaiskana brands.
markets: Sells in Sweden, Denmark, Norway and Finland to retailers and foodservice customers.
rationale: Nordic poultry brands with a regional focus and modest marketing budgets; F1 sponsorship appears poorly matched to its customers.

name: Cal-Maine Foods
desc: Largest US producer and distributor of fresh shell eggs, selling conventional, cage-free and specialty eggs.
markets: Sells eggs to US retailers and foodservice customers; no international footprint.
rationale: Commodity egg producer with little consumer marketing culture and a purely domestic customer base; very weak F1 fit and unlikely buyer.

name: Clearwater Paper
desc: Producer of private-label tissue for US retailers, including bath tissue, paper towels, facial tissue and napkins.
markets: Sells tissue mainly to US retailers and private-label customers; no international footprint or expansion plans are known.
rationale: B2B private-label manufacturer with no consumer brand and a purely domestic business; very weak F1 fit and unlikely buyer.

name: Co-operative Group
desc: UK consumer co-operative owned by members, running Co-op Food convenience stores, funeral care, insurance and legal services.
markets: Stores and services across the UK; no international operations.
rationale: Member-owned UK retailer with ethical positioning; F1's British Grand Prix gives some visibility, but fit is limited.

name: ECOM Agroindustrial
desc: Commodity merchant specialising in coffee, cocoa and cotton, buying and trading from farmers for global food and textile customers.
markets: Buys from farmers in producing countries and sells to customers in Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: B2B commodity trader with no consumer profile and farmer and manufacturer customers; weak F1 fit, though hospitality could help client relations.

name: COFCO International
desc: Agricultural trading and processing arm of state-owned COFCO Group, trading grains, oilseeds, sugar and cotton worldwide.
markets: Operations across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Black Sea, supplying China and other markets.
rationale: State-owned B2B commodity trader with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit, with some hospitality value for trading partners and Chinese ties.

name: Westrock Coffee Company
desc: Company that sources, roasts and processes coffee, tea and extracts for retailers, restaurants and beverage brands.
markets: Sources coffee globally and sells mainly to US retail and foodservice customers.
rationale: B2B coffee processor with limited consumer branding; F1 hospitality fit is modest.

name: MIDERA Food Processing
desc: Manufacturer of industrial food processing equipment, according to Crunchbase, based in Elk Grove Village, Illinois.
markets: Based in Illinois; customers and any international activity are not confirmed from the available data, so scale is unknown.
rationale: Industrial equipment maker with no known consumer brand and unconfirmed scale; an F1 partnership looks unlikely and the fit is weak.

name: Papa John's
desc: Pizza delivery and carryout chain with about 6,000 restaurants in nearly 50 countries, mostly franchised.
markets: Restaurants in the United States, the UK, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia, mostly franchised.
rationale: Consumer brand with sports sponsorship history; F1 could support promotions in the US and international markets.

name: Xingsheng Youxuan
desc: Community group-buying platform where residents order groceries and household goods online and collect them from neighbourhood stores.
markets: Operates in China through neighbourhood pickup stores and an app; no international operations or expansion plans are known.
rationale: Chinese community commerce platform with a domestic focus and thin margins; very weak F1 fit and unlikely buyer.

name: iFood
desc: Brazil's largest food delivery platform, connecting consumers with restaurants, supermarkets and pharmacies through an app.
markets: Operates across Brazil; no verified operations in other countries today.
rationale: Consumer app with huge Brazilian reach and sports sponsorship history; F1's Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers local visibility.

name: Hostess Brands
desc: US packaged baked goods brand, maker of Twinkies, Cupcakes, Ding Dongs and Donettes.
markets: Sells mainly to US retailers and consumers; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Nostalgic US snack brand now inside a larger group; F1 spend is unlikely.

name: Krispy Kreme
desc: Doughnut maker and retailer founded in 1937, selling Original Glazed and other treats through shops and grocery outlets.
markets: Shops and retail points in the United States, UK, Australia, Mexico, Japan and other countries.
rationale: Consumer brand with global stores and strong sampling culture; F1 could support fan promotions and hospitality treats.

name: Campari Group
desc: Italian spirits company owning Aperol, Campari, Wild Turkey, SKYY and Grand Marnier, sold worldwide.
markets: Sells across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific, with Aperol and Campari as key brands.
rationale: Premium aperitif brands suit hospitality and celebration moments; alcohol advertising rules limit some Grand Prix markets.

name: CBC (Central America Bottling Corporation)
desc: Guatemalan beverage company bottling PepsiCo drinks and local brands for Central America and the Caribbean.
markets: Bottles and distributes beverages across Central America and the Caribbean, with franchise restaurants and other businesses.
rationale: Strong regional beverage distribution; PepsiCo link could allow an F1 tie-in in Latin America.
f1: Bottler for PepsiCo, an F1 global partner

name: La Doria
desc: Italian producer of canned tomato products, prepared sauces, beverages and ready meals, largely supplying private-label retail customers.
markets: Based in Campania, Italy, supplying European retailers; export markets are not confirmed.
rationale: Mostly private-label B2B supplier with limited brand visibility; F1 hospitality could support customers, but fit is modest.

name: PepsiCo Mexico
desc: Mexican subsidiary of PepsiCo making and distributing Pepsi, Sabritas and Gamesa snacks and drinks across Mexico.
markets: Operates plants and distribution across Mexico, selling to shops and retailers.
rationale: Mass-market Mexican brand with the Mexico City Grand Prix as home race; parent PepsiCo is already an F1 partner.
f1: Parent PepsiCo is an F1 partner

name: Ahold Delhaize
desc: Dutch retail group owning Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Food Lion, Stop & Shop and Giant supermarkets in Europe and the US.
markets: Stores in the Netherlands, Belgium, other European countries and the United States, plus online retail.
rationale: Large grocery group with a loyalty base in Europe and the US; F1 could support promotions, though no motorsport link is known.

name: China Mengniu Dairy
desc: Chinese dairy producer selling Mengniu milk, Milk Deluxe, Future Star, yoghurt and ice cream across China.
markets: Sells mainly in China, with some overseas business in Southeast Asia.
rationale: Major Chinese consumer brand with sports sponsorship experience; F1's Shanghai race offers local visibility.

name: Chipotle Mexican Grill
desc: Fast-casual Mexican restaurant chain founded in Denver in 1993, selling burritos and bowls mainly in the US.
markets: Restaurants mainly in the United States, with locations in Canada, the UK, France and Germany.
rationale: Strong US consumer brand; F1's growing American audience could support promotions, though no motorsport link is known.

name: MGP Ingredients
desc: Producer of distilled spirits and specialty wheat proteins, supplying bourbon, whiskey and gin to brand owners and food makers.
markets: Plants in Kansas, Indiana and Kentucky supplying mainly US customers and brand owners.
rationale: Mostly B2B spirits supplier selling to brand owners with limited consumer awareness; weak F1 fit and alcohol advertising limits.

name: Nexture
desc: Italian food group, successor to Newlat Food, making and selling pasta, dairy, bakery and special-nutrition products.
markets: Operates in Italy and the UK through its food brands; no verified expansion plans into other regions are known.
rationale: Mid-sized food group with modest marketing budgets and a European customer base; F1 fit is limited.

name: Novus Foods
desc: Maker of refrigerated desserts, dips and snacks supplying retailers and foodservice customers, often under retailers' own labels.
markets: Based in Ohio; sells mainly to US retailers and foodservice customers.
rationale: Largely private-label supplier with little consumer recognition and a domestic customer base; weak F1 fit and unlikely buyer.

name: Patanjali Foods
desc: Indian edible oil and packaged food maker, formerly Ruchi Soya, controlled by the Patanjali Ayurved group.
markets: Sells across India, with some exports; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Well-known Indian consumer brand but domestic focus; F1 fit is limited without an Indian race.

name: Suedzucker
desc: German sugar and food group, Europe's largest sugar producer, with sugar, specialty ingredients, fruit and CropEnergies segments.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, with ingredients and other businesses sold worldwide.
rationale: B2B sugar and ingredient producer with limited consumer branding; weak F1 fit.

name: Smithfield Foods
desc: Pork producer and packaged meats company with brands including Smithfield, Eckrich and Nathan's Famous.
markets: Operations in the United States, Poland and Romania, selling to retailers and foodservice customers.
rationale: Large US meat brand with limited motorsport synergy; F1 fit is weak.

name: Lotte Group
desc: Korean-Japanese conglomerate active in confectionery, retail, hotels, theme parks, chemicals and food.
markets: Businesses in South Korea, Japan and other countries, including hotels and chemicals.
rationale: Consumer brands such as Lotte Hotels and confectionery could use F1 for hospitality and Asian visibility.

name: Dutch Bros Coffee
desc: Drive-through coffee chain founded in 1992 in Oregon, with over 1,000 shops serving coffee, energy drinks and teas.
markets: Shops across US states, mainly in the West and Southwest; no international presence.
rationale: US-focused coffee chain with a young customer base; F1's US races could support promotions, but fit is limited.

name: Restaurant Brands International
desc: Parent of Burger King, Tim Hortons, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs, franchising fast-food restaurants worldwide.
markets: Restaurants in over 120 countries across North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Global fast-food brands could use F1 for fan promotions and menu activations across many Grand Prix markets.

name: Pet Valu
desc: Canadian specialty retailer of pet food and supplies, with about 800 corporate and franchise stores.
markets: Stores across Canada only; no international operations or expansion plans are known for this domestic pet retailer.
rationale: Domestic pet retailer with limited marketing reach beyond Canada; weak F1 fit, though the Canadian Grand Prix gives some visibility.

name: Coca-Cola Beverages Florida
desc: Bottler and distributor of Coca-Cola products across much of Florida, supplying supermarkets, restaurants and convenience stores.
markets: Sells and delivers beverages within Florida to retailers and food service customers.
rationale: Regional bottler with Miami Grand Prix proximity but no standalone consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Athletic Brewing
desc: Connecticut brewer of non-alcoholic craft beer, with brands such as Run Wild IPA and Upside Dawn.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States; international expansion is not confirmed.
rationale: Brand-led non-alcoholic beer suits F1's focus on responsible drinking and sports audiences, especially in the US.

name: Mountaintop Beverage
desc: West Virginia contract manufacturer producing aseptic and extended-shelf-life beverages, including dairy, plant-based and protein drinks.
markets: Customers are US food and beverage brands and retailers; no international activity known.
rationale: B2B co-packer with no consumer brand of its own; weak F1 fit.

name: Guming
desc: Chinese milk tea chain founded in 2010 in Zhejiang, selling tea drinks made with fresh fruit and milk.
markets: Stores across China, mainly through franchised outlets; no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Youth-oriented drink brand with domestic focus; F1's Shanghai race could support promotions, but fit is limited.

name: iD Fresh Food
desc: Indian packaged-food company making fresh ready-to-cook idli and dosa batter, parotas and other chilled foods.
markets: Sells in India, with operations in the Middle East and the United States.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer food brand; F1 could help brand awareness among Indian diaspora, but marketing budgets are modest.

name: Zevia
desc: Beverage company selling zero-calorie, zero-sugar soda sweetened with stevia in many flavours.
markets: Sells in the United States and Canada through retailers and online.
rationale: Health-oriented US beverage brand targeting younger consumers; F1's US growth offers awareness, but its budget is limited.

name: San Miguel Corporation
desc: Philippine conglomerate founded in 1890 with interests in food and beverage, energy, fuel, infrastructure and airports.
markets: Operations centred on the Philippines, with some overseas investments; no verified new expansion plans.
rationale: Large Philippine conglomerate with sponsorship budgets, but F1 has no Philippine race and operations are domestic.

name: Cefetra Group
desc: Rotterdam-based international trader and supplier of food and feed ingredients, including grains, oilseeds and proteins.
markets: Trades and supplies ingredients between producing countries and customers in Europe and other regions.
rationale: B2B commodity trader with no consumer brand and food and feed industry customers; weak F1 fit, with limited hospitality value.

name: Chefs' Warehouse
desc: US specialty food distributor supplying premium ingredients to chefs and restaurants.
markets: Distribution centres in the United States and Canada, with some Middle East presence.
rationale: B2B distributor to high-end restaurants; F1 hospitality could suit client entertainment, but it lacks a consumer brand.

name: SalMar
desc: Norwegian salmon farmer, one of the world's largest, producing Atlantic and organic salmon for global markets.
markets: Farms in Norway and Iceland, selling salmon to customers in Europe, Asia and North America.
rationale: B2B seafood producer with limited consumer branding; F1 hospitality fit is modest.

name: Compass Group
desc: World's largest contract catering company, providing food and support services to businesses, hospitals, schools and events.
markets: Operates in about 45 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: B2B hospitality provider with event catering strength; F1 hospitality and fan food services offer a natural fit.

name: Impossible Foods
desc: Plant-based food company founded in 2011, making Impossible Burger and other meat alternatives for retailers and restaurants.
markets: Sells in the United States and in markets such as Canada, Hong Kong, Singapore and the UK.
rationale: Brand-led plant-based company with sustainability story that could fit F1's net-zero messaging and young fans.

name: Ferrero
desc: Confectionery group making Nutella, Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella biscuits, founded in Alba, Italy.
markets: Sells in over 170 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Global family-owned consumer brands with strong marketing; F1 could support product launches and fan promotions.

name: Greencross
desc: Australasian specialist pet care retailer and vet operator, with Petbarn and City Farmers stores and Greencross Vets clinics.
markets: Stores and vet clinics in Australia and New Zealand.
rationale: Australian pet care brand with local focus; F1's Melbourne race gives some visibility, but regional scale limits fit.
changed: Taken private by TPG Capital in 2019

name: Toast
desc: Restaurant technology company selling cloud-based point-of-sale, payments and software to restaurants.
markets: Serves restaurants mainly in the United States, with operations in Canada, the UK, Ireland and Australia.
rationale: Software brand targeting restaurants and hospitality, which suits F1's hospitality and food partners and a technology showcase.
